sections.h2: How a home sale works in Hempfield Township
sections.html:
Paperwork is lighter in Hempfield than in many Pennsylvania municipalities, because the township does not ask for a certificate of occupancy at sale. What you do need is a clear picture of your septic or sewer setup, the 2 percent transfer tax and the county assessment record.

Hempfield is a large Westmoreland County township, spread over about 77 square miles, with an estimated 41,421 residents. Population is steady rather than growing, so sellers mostly compete with other established houses. About 84.7 percent of homes are owner-occupied, a typical owned home is valued at $232,100, and typical rent is $964. More than a quarter of residents are 65 or older, and that mix is why estate sales and downsizing moves are common.

However the buyer finds you, the deed ends up at the Westmoreland County Recorder of Deeds in Greensburg, where the deed is filed and the transfer tax is paid.

The city of Greensburg and six boroughs sit entirely inside the township: Southwest Greensburg, South Greensburg, Youngwood, New Stanton, Arona and Adamsburg. Communities within it include Fort Allen, Grapeville, Hannastown, Carbon, Radebaugh, Maplewood Terrace, West Point and Luxor. The township is big enough that a home near Greensburg and a rural parcel miles away can have very different values.

Hempfield is the retail center for the Laurel Highlands, with U.S. Route 30 passing the Westmoreland Mall and Greengate Centre. The Hempfield Area School District serves the township.

A tornado on March 23, 2011 damaged many homes in the West Hempfield area and the Fort Allen neighborhood. A buyer may ask whether a house in those areas needed storm repairs, so have the answer ready.

sections.h2: Local rules when a Hempfield house sells
sections.html:
The township's planning and code department says a certificate of occupancy is not required to sell a home. Two other checks apply, depending on how the house drains.

  • On-lot septic. Contact the township's Sewage Enforcement Officer about any dye test the buyer or lender wants.
  • Public sewer. Call the Municipal Authority of Westmoreland County at 724-755-5800 for the sewer account and any test or final reading.
  • Permits. Sort out open permits and unpermitted work first. Zoning permits take up to 15 business days and building permits up to 30.

The code office is at 1132 Woodward Drive, Suite A, and answers at 724-834-7232. The county assessment office, at 724-830-3409, can explain whether a building permit changes the assessed value. Landlord and tenant disputes go to the Pennsylvania Attorney General's consumer hotline at 1-800-441-2555.

Township property tax is low in dollar terms. The township levies 3 mills for general purposes and 3 mills for a dedicated fire service tax. School and county taxes are separate and larger. Areas inside a street light district also pay a yearly light district assessment. The township runs a rebate program that returns part of the general township real estate tax to qualifying senior homeowners, which long-time owners of older houses may already use.

The full charge on a sale is 2 percent of the price. It is paid when the deed is recorded, and the recorder can be reached at 724-830-3518.

Who receives the 2 percent Hempfield transfer tax

Your sales contract says who covers which share, and both parties answer to the recorder for the tax. State rules exempt certain family transfers and property passing by inheritance.

Have the title company show you the transfer tax line before signing. If you are selling an inherited house, ask whether the inheritance exemption covers your deed.

sections.h2: How do Westmoreland County assessment appeals work?
sections.html:
The county Tax Assessment Office sets the values that drive every property tax bill in the township. Anyone can appeal a change of assessment within 40 days of the mailing of the notice. A yearly appeal has to be on file by August 1 and only changes the next tax year's bill.

Hearings run on the second Thursday of every month, starting at 9:00 in the morning, in Suite 440 of the county building at 40 North Pennsylvania Avenue in Greensburg. Forms come from the county website or the assessment office itself.

If you plan to sell, check the assessed value before you list. Lenders look at the current tax amount. If you think the assessment is too high, file by the next August 1.

sections.h2: From listing to deed: what to prepare
sections.html:
A Hempfield sale goes more smoothly when you settle a few questions in advance. Know whether the house is on septic or public sewer, because that decides who you call for a dye test or a final reading. Find out whether any permit was left open or any work was done without one. Pull your current tax bills and any street light district assessment, since the buyer's title company will prorate them at settlement.

When an offer comes in, the title company orders the search, the contract names who pays each share of the transfer tax, and the deed goes to the Recorder of Deeds in Greensburg once you sign at closing. If a parent's estate is involved, have the paperwork showing who may sign ready before you accept an offer, because that is the item most likely to slow things down.

Keep a simple folder with the sewer account number, the code office phone number, your permit history and the county assessment notice. When a buyer or lender asks a question, you can answer it the same day instead of making calls while the closing date drifts closer.

sections.h2: Which Hempfield houses suit a direct cash sale?
sections.html:
A cash sale tends to suit worn houses, estate properties and sellers who want to pick the closing date. It is less useful for a move-in-ready home you can list quickly.

Set any cash figure against what a listing would net after commission, transfer tax, repairs and months of waiting. If you want to see a number for your Hempfield house, Cash Home Buyers CA can quote one, and you can set it beside your other choices.

A cash sale skips showings, a buyer's loan approval and most repair negotiation. You still deal with the same local items: the septic or sewer check, any open permits, the transfer tax and the recorder's filing. Ask the buyer to confirm in writing which of those they will handle, so nothing is left to the last week before closing.

A house inherited from a parent is a common fit. The heirs often live elsewhere, the property sat for a while, and nobody wants to manage repairs from a distance. Picking the closing date yourself lets the estate wrap up on its own schedule, with no lender deadline hanging over the heirs.

faqs.q: Is a certificate of occupancy needed for a Hempfield home sale?
faqs.a: No. The township's planning and code office confirms that the sale of a home does not trigger a certificate of occupancy.

faqs.q: Who handles a dye test for a Hempfield home sale?
faqs.a: It depends on the system. For a septic system, contact the township's Sewage Enforcement Officer. For public sewer, call the Municipal Authority of Westmoreland County at 724-755-5800.

faqs.q: Who gets the 2 percent Hempfield transfer tax?
faqs.a: The state receives 1 percent, the township 0.5 percent and the Hempfield Area School District 0.5 percent. The county recorder in Greensburg collects the money when the deed goes on record.

faqs.q: Which school district covers Hempfield Township?
faqs.a: The Hempfield Area School District. It also covers Adamsburg, Armbrust, Bovard, Grapeville, Hunker, Luxor, Manor, New Stanton and Youngwood.

faqs.q: When must a Westmoreland County assessment appeal be filed?
faqs.a: August 1 for a yearly appeal, which affects the following tax year. If a change of assessment notice is mailed, the window is 40 days.
